messages:
incident-bot: Paging: high error and tail latency spike in kvstore-continuous-batcher across us-west-2 clusters. Thresholds crossed: 99th latency > 2s, error rate +3% for the last 6m. Auto-escalation to oncall-sre.
elaine: @oncall-sre got the page, joining. Seeing big queuing in batch-scheduler metrics.
sam: I can reproduce in staging — lots of tiny requests blocking long-running batches. Looks like continuous batching is coalescing long tails and causing KV cache to grow and trigger paging.
taylor: Are we seeing cache eviction churn? I see the cached key count jump then massive disk I/O.
kevin: Logs from one host: 
```
kvstore: cache_size=3.2GB num_entries=1.2M evictions/sec=4200 paging=true
batcher: inflight_batches=128 avg_batch_time=750ms max=3.2s
sched: queue_depth_short=230 queue_depth_long=12
```
chris: wow, eviction/sec that high. Could be kvprefetch prefilling lots of entries for long requests. Customer-facing tail would explain increased 5xxs.
elaine: Immediate mitigation options: 1) temporarily disable continuous prefix prefetching; 2) reduce max_coalesce_time on batcher to favor short requests; 3) bump eviction threshold to avoid thrash. Which one is safest to try first?
oncall-sre: Recommend lowering max_coalesce_time to 10ms and enabling a pack_shed flag to prevent big requests from monopolizing. Rolling that now to us-west-2-canary.
kevin: Pushing the canary patch: 
```
# quick patch
set-config batcher.max_coalesce_time=10ms
set-config batcher.pack_shed=true
deploy service batch-scheduler --env us-west-2 --tag hotfix/pack-shed-2141592653
```
pm-anna: Noted customer impact: a few high-traffic customers on Dedicated reported slow responses — CS is already triaging. Marking this P1 and adding to incident timeline.
sam: Canary show reduction in 99th from 2.2s -> 0.8s on canary nodes, eviction/sec down from 4200 -> 1200. Rolling to 50% now.
chris: Also seeing decreased KV paging IO. Great. I'll keep an eye on long-tail jobs though.
elaine: After 50% rollout, tail latency across region dropped to ~700ms. Error rate near baseline. Rolling full.
taylor (typo name corrected): (reacts :thumbsup:)
kevin: Full rollout complete at +32m. Post-rollout metrics: 99th 0.6-0.9s, error spike cleared.
pm-anna: Customer note: affected customers had brief degradation ~30-40m window. CS to email with summary and mitigation timeline.
oncall-sre: Root cause hypothesis: continuous batching + aggressive prefetch for long requests produced a working set blowup in the KV cache, causing eviction storms and paging. The batch scheduler then unfairly favored forming big batches, starving short requests and amplifying tail latency.
sam: Action items: 1) create follow-up ticket to add request-size-aware fairness in scheduler; 2) add backpressure circuit when cache eviction exceeds threshold; 3) add a canary rule to auto-reduce coalesce_time when eviction/sec > 1000.
chris: I'm on the scheduler fairness ticket. Will prototype weighted queueing by request-size and an emergency demux for short requests.
kevin: I'll open the eviction-backpressure PR and metrics alerts for eviction/sec and paging latency.
elaine: Oncall handoff in 2h to @taylor. I'll document the hotfix and attach logs.
pm-anna: Filing customer postmortem draft; will coordinate wording with eng.
oncall-sre: Leaving the channel but monitoring. Ping me if rollback needed.
elaine: Thanks everyone. Quick follow-up note for the record: commands we ran and dashboard urls.
```
# commands
kubectl -n redwood rollout restart deploy/batch-scheduler -l region=us-west-2
hk patch config batcher --set max_coalesce_time=10ms --set pack_shed=true
# dashboards
https://metrics.redwood.internal/d/kv/kv-paging?orgId=1&var-region=us-west-2
https://metrics.redwood.internal/d/bs/batcher-99th?orgId=1&var-region=us-west-2
```
kevin: tagging follow-ups: INF-4274 (scheduler fairness), INF-4275 (eviction-backpressure), DOC-312 (customer timeline).
sam: Also adding regression test for mixed tiny+huge workload in our nightly perf harness.
elaine: Closing incident thread in 24h unless regressions. Will attach final incident timeline once CS email goes out.
pm-anna: Thanks all.
